h1: Launching a spirits brand in India from abroad
title: Launching a Spirits Brand in India | Craft Beer School
desc: How a foreign spirits brand can launch in India: import, bottle in India or licence production, with state rules, duties, labels and distribution in outline.
teaser: India is a large whisky drinking country. That does not mean an outside brand finds the door open.
standfirst: A foreign spirits brand enters India by importing, bottling in India or licensing local production. This guide explains each route, the state rules around them and the questions to ask first.
sections:
Import means shipping finished bottles. You keep control of the liquid and the packaging. Duties and state treatment of imported spirits often make the shelf price high.

Bottling in India means you ship bulk spirit and bottle locally. It may reduce cost, subject to rules on how bulk spirit moves and what the label may say. States may treat the result differently from finished imports. Ask your adviser, because this changes by state and over time.

Licensed production means an Indian distiller makes and sells under your brand. It can bring local scale but needs strong control of quality and of the brand.
Why the state matters more than the brand

Alcohol is a state subject. Each state sets licences, excise duty, pricing, brand registration, label approval and the way spirits are sold. These rules vary widely and change. Several states, including Bihar and Gujarat, have prohibition. Some states sell through government-run outlets. Others license private retailers.

Imports also face central customs duty and import registration. The sum of central and state charges is a main driver of price. Ask your licensing adviser for current figures state by state. We do not quote rates because they change.
Product, price and the Indian drinker

Indian whisky is a large category with deep roots in local taste. A foreign brand needs a clear reason for being on the shelf: provenance, style, age statement or a new occasion. Premium positioning means a high price, which narrows the audience.

Gin and other lighter spirits have found a place in bars and with younger drinkers. Our guides on selling gin direct and a flavoured gin business case look at how a gin business is built. Test your product with Indian drinkers before you scale, as described in market research in India for a foreign drinks brand.

Labels must follow central labelling rules and may need approval in each state. Brand names may need registering with the state authority before sale. Register your trademark in India early.

Advertising of alcohol is tightly restricted in India. Many brands use events, tastings in licensed venues and brand experiences rather than direct advertising. Take legal advice on what is allowed and always market responsibly, with no targeting of minors.

Heat matters for aged spirits. Evaporation in India is well above that in cool climates. Maturation runs faster. If you plan to age in India, your cask programme will differ from the one at home. Imported aged spirit is already finished and only needs sensible storage.

Bonded storage rules vary by state. Keep records of every movement, since the excise authority will want them.

We do not guarantee licences, partners or sales and we do not name clients. Read also finding an Indian partner for a drinks brand.

Few foreign spirits brands enter India alone. A local partner may hold licences, run distribution and know which outlets matter. The terms of the partnership decide who owns the brand, who controls pricing and what happens if either side leaves.

Check the partner's licences and history before you talk terms. Visit if you can. Ask other brands they work with how they find the relationship. Our guide on finding an Indian partner covers the checks in more detail.

Put quality in the agreement. The partner should accept your right to inspect, sample and reject. A weak batch under your name will cost you more than it costs them.

Agree how you will both handle a complaint, a recall or a regulator's question. These are rare, but sorting out the process in a calm month is far easier than doing it during a crisis.

Finally, agree how the partnership ends. Exit terms feel awkward to discuss at the start, but a clear exit protects a brand that took years to build.
faqs: Is it cheaper to bottle in India?
It can be, but state rules on bulk spirit and labelling vary. Ask a licensing adviser before you assume a saving.
Can I advertise a spirits brand in India?
Alcohol advertising is tightly restricted. Take legal advice on what is allowed and market responsibly.
Which state should I start in?
That depends on rules, route to market and your product. See our guide on choosing an Indian state.
